speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing confusion, abdominal pain, and vomiting; tell me, how long have these symptoms been present and have you noticed any fever or change in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) precipitated by post-gastrectomy gastroparesis and possible foodborne illness. The combination of recent sleeve gastrectomy, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, and new-onset confusion in a diabetic patient is highly suggestive of metabolic acidosis from DKA, potentially triggered by an infectious gastroenteritis or food intolerance causing poor oral intake and dehydration. I will confirm this with blood work immediately. REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, Serum Glucose, Beta-hydroxybutyrate, Arterial Blood Gas.
